sections.text: Programs often need to choose what to do. if runs some code only when a condition is true. else runs when it isn't.
A condition is a question with a true-or-false answer. Common comparisons are > (greater than), < (less than), >= (at least), <= (at most), == (equal to) and != (not equal to).
Watch out: one = stores a value, two == compares values. if age == 18 asks a question; let age = 18 sets the value.
Use else if to check more than two cases. Rust checks them from top to bottom and runs only the first one that's true:
